options.text: Makes a component render on the server
Lazy-loads a component in its own chunk, fetched on first render

questions.explanation: defineAsyncComponent wraps a dynamic import so the component's code is split into a chunk loaded only when it's first rendered — shrinking the initial bundle.

questions.prompt: By default, what happens to a component's state when you toggle it off with v-if and back on?

options.text: The component is destroyed and recreated, losing its state — unless wrapped in <KeepAlive>

questions.explanation: v-if truly removes and recreates the component (losing state). <KeepAlive> caches the instance so state and DOM persist across toggles.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between v-once and v-memo?

options.text: v-once renders a subtree once and never updates it; v-memo re-renders only when its listed dependencies change
v-memo renders once; v-once memoizes deps

questions.explanation: v-once freezes a subtree after the first render; v-memo="[deps]" conditionally skips re-rendering unless a dependency changes.

questions.prompt: A kept-alive component fires the onActivated and on______ hooks when shown and hidden. (complete the word)
questions.explanation: Inside <KeepAlive>, components use onActivated (shown) and onDeactivated (hidden) instead of mounted/unmounted.

questions.prompt: What is the main risk of using v-memo with an incomplete dependency array?

options.text: Stale UI — Vue skips updates for changes not listed in the deps

questions.explanation: v-memo only re-renders when a listed dependency changes. If a value the subtree uses isn't in the deps, its changes won't show — a stale UI.

questions.prompt: Which are legitimate everyday performance practices in Vue? Select all that apply.

options.text: Use computed for cached derived values

questions.explanation: Stable keys, cached computeds, and a production build are solid defaults. v-once freezes updates, so blanketing everything with it would break dynamic UI.
